mainTopic: Who is liable for acting on בית דין's mistaken ruling: the judge or תלמיד who knew better, the משנה's general rule, and the מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and חכמים
overview: The amud first finishes a question about the order of cases in the משנה. Then it asks why the משנה lists both a judge who knew בית דין erred and a תלמיד ראוי להוראה. רבא explains that the extra case teaches that even someone who is only learned (גמיר), or only sharp (סביר), is liable for acting on his own knowledge. He names שמעון בן עזאי and שמעון בן זומא as examples. אביי objects that such great scholars would be sinning on purpose (מזיד). רבא answers that their mistake was thinking they must obey the חכמים even when the חכמים are wrong. Next the גמרא explains what each half of the משנה's general rule (זה הכלל) comes to include. Finally, שמואל says the משנה follows רבי יהודה, while חכמים hold that an individual who follows בית דין's ruling is חייב. The גמרא proves from the ברייתא's structure that, for חכמים, a minority who followed a ruling brings its own קרבן. It then starts to show why the first ברייתא belongs to רבי יהודה, and that proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The later cases follow a 'this, and certainly that' order
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers an earlier question about the order of cases in the משנה. It says the תנא lists them in a 'this, and needless to say that' style.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches in the style of 'this case, and there is no need to say that case.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question from just before about why the משנה lists its cases in this order. The answer is that it uses a 'this, and certainly that' style.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this style, the משנה states one case and expects you to realize that the next case is even more obvious. So the order is deliberate and not a mistake. This closes the earlier question about the order of the cases.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This, and there is no need to say that': a style where each case is more obvious than the one before
He (the תנא) teaches

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר זוֹ קָתָנֵי.
phrases.english: He teaches: this, and there is no need to say that.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר זוֹ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question from the preceding section of the daf about the order of cases
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the literary style of the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: The order is intentional. Each later case is more obvious than the one before it.

steps.title: Why does the משנה list two similar cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a judge who knew בית דין erred, or a תלמיד ראוי להוראה, and asks why both are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And one of them knew that they erred, or a student who is fit to issue rulings.' Why do I need both of these?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה. It asks why the משנה needs two cases, since a qualified תלמיד seems the same as one of the judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both people knew enough to see that בית דין's ruling was wrong. So one case should seem to be enough. The גמרא challenges the extra case as if it were unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: That they (בית דין) made a mistake
A student who is not one of the judges
Fit to issue halachic rulings
Why do I need two (cases)?

phrases.english: And one of them knew that they erred
phrases.notes: 'One of them' means one of the judges of בית דין that gave the mistaken ruling.

phrases.english: or a student who is fit to issue rulings.
Why do I need two?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of both a judge and a qualified student
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A qualified student is the same as a judge who knew the ruling was wrong, so one of the cases looks redundant.

steps.title: רבא: The second case is needed for a different kind of scholar
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both cases are needed. Otherwise we might think only someone who is both learned and analytical is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It was necessary. You might have thought this rule applies only to someone who is learned and analytical, but someone who is learned and not analytical would not be liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends the משנה. He says the second case is needed so that we don't limit the rule to only the top kind of scholar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא names two skills: גמיר (knowing a lot of learning) and סביר (being able to reason things through). Without the second case, we might think only someone with both skills is liable for acting on his own. The extra case widens the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
It would enter your mind to say (a mistaken first thought)
Learned; knows a lot of material
Analytical; able to reason things through

phrases.english: Rava said: It was necessary,
for it would enter your mind to say
these words apply to one who is learned and analytical,
phrases.notes: 'These words' means the rule that he is liable for acting on his own.

phrases.english: but one who is learned and not analytical, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why two cases are needed
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each case teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only someone who is both גמיר and סביר would be liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even someone who is גמיר but not סביר is liable.

steps.title: אביי: 'Fit to rule' already means fully skilled
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that the phrase ראוי להוראה itself implies someone who is both learned and analytical.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: 'Fit to issue rulings' means someone who is learned and analytical!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's answer. He points out that the very words of the second case describe a top-level scholar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the second case adds a scholar who is less than fully skilled. But the משנה calls him ראוי להוראה, and a person fit to issue rulings needs both skills. So the second case can't be adding a weaker scholar.

keyTerms.meaning: It implies; it means

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
'To issue rulings' implies learned and analytical!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: לְהוֹרָאָה גְּמִיר וּסְבִיר מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the student case covers someone who is not fully skilled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words ראוי להוראה themselves describe someone who is both גמיר and סביר, so they can't teach a case of a less skilled person.

steps.title: רבא clarifies: The extra case teaches that even half-skilled scholars count
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the judge case alone would suggest only full scholars are liable. The extra, seemingly unneeded student case teaches that someone with only one of the two skills is also included.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what I am saying. If we only had that first case, I would have said the rule applies only to someone learned and analytical, but someone learned and not analytical would not be liable. So the משנה taught 'fit to issue rulings,' and from this extra case we learn: even learned and not analytical, or analytical and not learned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains what he really meant. The lesson does not come from the words ראוי להוראה themselves. It comes from the fact that the משנה added a case it did not seem to need.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי is right that ראוי להוראה sounds like a full scholar. But since that case adds nothing beyond the judge case, its extra presence tells us to widen the rule. Now it includes גמיר without סביר, and also סביר without גמיר.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what I am saying (clarifying my words)
From an extra, seemingly unneeded part of the משנה
I would have said (a mistaken first thought)

steps.whatToRemember: The extra case of the תלמיד ראוי להוראה teaches, as a משנה יתירה, that a person is liable even if he has only one of the two skills: learning (גמיר) or reasoning (סביר).
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is NOT saying the words ראוי להוראה mean a half-skilled person. He agrees with אביי about what the words mean. The lesson comes from the fact that the case is extra.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what I am saying:
if from that one, I would have said
phrases.notes: 'That one' means the first case, the judge who knew בית דין erred.

phrases.english: these words apply to one who is learned and analytical,
but one who is learned and not analytical, no,
so he taught 'fit to issue rulings,'
and from the extra part of the משנה we learn:
even one who is learned and not analytical,
or analytical and not learned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's objection by clarifying רבא's original point
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarification: the lesson comes from the case being extra, not from its wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the judge case alone, only a person who is both גמיר and סביר would be liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the student case is extra, the rule also covers someone who is גמיר but not סביר, or סביר but not גמיר.

steps.title: Who is an example of someone fit to rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes ראוי להוראה from the משנה and asks for an example of such a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Fit to issue rulings,' etc. Like whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question about the same words in the משנה. It asks for a concrete example of someone who is ראוי להוראה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא discussed why this case is in the משנה at all. Now it wants to define who actually fits the description. This sets up רבא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the quote from the משנה continues
Like whom? (asking for an example)

phrases.english: 'Fit to issue rulings,' etc.
Like whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question on the same phrase of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A real example of a person who counts as ראוי להוראה

steps.title: רבא: Like שמעון בן עזאי and שמעון בן זומא
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives the examples of שמעון בן עזאי and שמעון בן זומא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Like שמעון בן עזאי and שמעון בן זומא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. He names two famous great scholars as examples of people who are ראוי להוראה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two were among the greatest scholars of their time, yet they are being described as 'students' rather than judges. So רבא is defining ראוי להוראה as a very high level of scholarship.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: כְּגוֹן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן עַזַּאי
phrases.english: Rava said: Like Shimon ben Azzai
and Shimon ben Zoma.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כְּגוֹן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן עַזַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of who counts as ראוי להוראה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Scholars on the level of שמעון בן עזאי and שמעון בן זומא

steps.title: אביי: A scholar that great would be acting on purpose
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that someone as great as these scholars would not make such a mistake, so he would count as a מזיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: In a case like this, he is acting on purpose!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's examples. He argues that such great scholars would not really be fooled by the wrong ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's case is about someone who acted by mistake, which is why he would bring a קרבן. A scholar like בן עזאי would surely know the ruling was wrong. So if he acted on it, he did it on purpose (מזיד), and that does not fit a case of bringing a קרבן for a mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case like this
Someone who sins on purpose, not by mistake

steps.confusionAlert: Being called a מזיד here does not mean he gets off easier. It means his act is no longer a mistake, so the rules for a mistaken act do not apply to him.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
In a case like this, he is acting on purpose!
phrases.notes: אביי means a scholar that great could not honestly make this mistake, so his act counts as deliberate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא מֵזִיד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's examples
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's examples of שמעון בן עזאי and שמעון בן זומא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Such great scholars could not honestly make this mistake, so their act would be deliberate (מזיד), not a mistake that requires a קרבן.

steps.title: רבא turns the challenge back on אביי with a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא cites a ברייתא that also treats a student like שמעון בן עזאי as liable, so אביי's objection hits the ברייתא too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your logic, what about the ברייתא: 'When he does it, one.' An individual who acts on his own is liable; one who acts on the ruling of בית דין is exempt. How so? If בית דין ruled that חלב is permitted, and one of the judges knew they erred, or a student sitting before them who is ראוי להוראה, like שמעון בן עזאי, might you think he is exempt? The פסוק says 'When he does it, one': an individual acting on his own is liable, but one acting on בית דין's ruling is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי's objection by pointing to a ברייתא that has the very same 'problem'. The ברייתא also calls a scholar like שמעון בן עזאי liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said a great scholar would not make such a mistake, so he would be a מזיד. רבא shows that a ברייתא names שמעון בן עזאי as liable for a קרבן, which means he counts as a שוגג. Whatever answer אביי gives for the ברייתא, רבא can use for his own words.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: a way of turning an objection back on the one who raised it
'When he does it, one' (ויקרא 4:27): the source that an individual acting on his own is liable
On his own authority
Forbidden fat
'You might think': it raises a possibility that is about to be rejected

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as רבא giving up his position. He is showing that אביי's objection would also knock out an accepted ברייתא, so it cannot be a real argument against רבא alone.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, that which is taught:
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבא, answering אביי's objection from the last step.

phrases.english: "When he does it, one",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:27

phrases.english: an individual who acts on his own is liable,
one who acts on the ruling of the court is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיצַד? הוֹרוּ בֵּית דִּין שֶׁחֵלֶב מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: How so? The court ruled that forbidden fat is permitted,
and it became known to one of them that they erred,
or a student sitting before them

phrases.aramaic: וְרָאוּי לְהוֹרָאָה כְּגוֹן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן עַזַּאי,
phrases.english: who is qualified to rule, such as Shimon ben Azzai,
might you think he would be exempt?
The verse says: "When he does it, one",

phrases.aramaic: יָחִיד הָעוֹשֶׂה עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ – חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: an individual who acts on his own is liable,
one who acts on the ruling of the court is exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counter-challenge to אביי's קשיא in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that a great scholar who sins would be a מזיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא calls a scholar like שמעון בן עזאי liable for a קרבן, so such a scholar can be a שוגג. אביי's objection would knock out the ברייתא too.

steps.title: How can such a case happen?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks how the ברייתא's case of a great scholar being a שוגג can actually happen.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, how can you find such a case?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks how the ברייתא's case works, since a great scholar who knows the ruling is wrong seems like a מזיד. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides now face the same puzzle: how can a scholar who knows the truth be called a שוגג? Whatever explains the ברייתא will also explain רבא's examples.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you find it? It asks for a realistic case

phrases.english: Rather, how can you find it?
phrases.notes: He means: how can the ברייתא's case of a learned שוגג ever happen?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the ברייתא cited in step 9 can be explained
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A realistic case where a scholar who knows the truth is still considered a שוגג

steps.title: He knew it was forbidden but erred about obeying the Sages
steps.stepSummary: The scholar knew the act was forbidden. His mistake was thinking there is a מצוה to follow the חכמים even when they are wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, where he knew it was forbidden, but he erred about the מצוה to listen to the words of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that the scholar's mistake was not about the law itself. He mistakenly believed he must obey בית דין even when he knows they are wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scholar knows חלב is forbidden, so he is not mistaken about the איסור. He is mistaken about the duty to obey the חכמים, and that mistake makes him a שוגג. This explains how even someone like שמעון בן עזאי can bring a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה to obey the words of the חכמים
He erred

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that being a שוגג does not require not knowing the law. A mistake about whether one must obey בית דין is also enough.

phrases.english: For example, where he knew that it is forbidden,
but he erred regarding the מצוה
to listen to the words of the Sages.
phrases.notes: He thought he had to follow the Sages even when he was sure they were mistaken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The scholar knew the act was forbidden but wrongly thought he was obligated to follow the חכמים anyway

steps.title: The same answer works for רבא's examples
steps.stepSummary: רבא uses the same explanation for שמעון בן עזאי and שמעון בן זומא, and this answers אביי's objection.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to me too, they erred about the מצוה to listen to the words of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא says his own examples work the same way as the ברייתא. This closes his answer to אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי claimed such great scholars would be מזידין. Their mistake was about obeying the חכמים, not about the law, so they are שוגגין. רבא's examples therefore stand.

keyTerms.meaning: According to me too

steps.whatToRemember: Even a top scholar like שמעון בן עזאי can be a liable שוגג. He knows the law, but he wrongly thinks he must still obey בית דין's mistaken ruling.

phrases.english: According to me too,
it is where they erred regarding the מצוה to listen to the words of the Sages.
phrases.notes: 'They' means שמעון בן עזאי and שמעון בן זומא from step 7.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the answer of step 11 to רבא's own examples, which resolves step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the scholar's mistake was about obeying the חכמים, not about the law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Great scholars cannot be שוגגין, so they would be מזידין
steps.terutzMaskana: Their mistake about the duty to obey the חכמים makes them שוגגין, so they are liable for a קרבן

steps.title: What does 'one who relies on himself' come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's general rule, התולה בעצמו חייב, and asks what extra case it adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This is the rule: one who relies on himself is liable.' What does it come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה, the general rule (זה הכלל). It asks what case this rule adds beyond the cases already listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זה הכלל usually comes to add cases that were not stated openly. The גמרא wants to know which new case this first half of the rule covers.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
One who relies on himself, acting on his own judgment
What does it come to include?

phrases.english: This is the principle: one who relies on himself is liable.
What does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: explaining the משנה's general rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which extra case the first half of the general rule adds

steps.title: It includes one who scorns rulings
steps.stepSummary: The first half of the rule adds the מבעט בהוראה, someone who looks down on rulings and relies only on himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It includes one who scorns rulings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule adds a person who looks down on בית דין's rulings in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This person did not act because בית דין told him to. He acts on his own view and does not care about rulings at all. So even when בית דין happens to permit something, he is still 'relying on himself' and is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: One who scorns rulings and kicks them aside

phrases.english: To include one who scorns rulings.
phrases.notes: Literally 'kicks at' rulings. He means someone who brushes off rulings and does whatever he thinks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule includes the מבעט בהוראה

steps.title: 'One who relies on the court' includes a ruling that was reversed
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the rule adds a case where בית דין ruled, realized its mistake, and reversed itself. Someone who acted on the first ruling is still exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who relies on בית דין' comes to include a case where בית דין ruled, realized they erred, and took the ruling back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half of the general rule the same way, by naming the extra case it adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose בית דין has already reversed its ruling, but a person acted on the original ruling. He still relied on בית דין, so he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: One who relies on בית דין
They took back their ruling

phrases.english: One who relies on the court —
to include where the court ruled
and they knew that they erred and retracted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same 'what does it include' question to the second half of the rule
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule includes a case where בית דין reversed its ruling but the person acted on the original ruling

steps.title: But that case is taught openly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this case is already stated openly elsewhere in the משנה, so the rule should not need to hint at it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches this case explicitly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer. The משנה states this case openly later on, so why would the rule be needed to add it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A general rule is supposed to add something new. If the reversed-ruling case appears openly in a later משנה, using the rule to include it looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Explicitly, openly

phrases.english: But it teaches it explicitly!
phrases.notes: It refers to a later משנה that states this case openly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the second half of the rule comes to include a ruling that was reversed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case is stated openly elsewhere in the משנה, so the rule would not need to add it

steps.title: It hints first, then explains
steps.stepSummary: The תנא first hints at the case in the general rule and later spells it out openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He teaches it, and then explains it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תנא can hint at a case first and spell it out later. This ends the section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating a case is not a problem when the first mention is only a hint inside a general rule. The later, open statement explains what the hint meant, so step 15's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches it in a general way, then explains it in detail

steps.whatToRemember: זה הכלל has two halves. 'Relying on himself' adds the מבעט בהוראה, who is liable. 'Relying on בית דין' adds someone who acted on a ruling that was later reversed, who is exempt.

phrases.english: He teaches it, and then explains it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Style of teaching: a hint first, an open statement later
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Including the case in the rule is pointless, since it is stated openly later
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule hints at it first, and the later משנה spells it out

steps.title: שמואל: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, but the Sages disagree
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the משנה's exemption for someone who follows בית דין is only רבי יהודה's view; חכמים say he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: This is the view of רבי יהודה. But חכמים say: an individual who acted on the ruling of בית דין is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל tells us that the משנה's ruling is not unanimous. It is one side of a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said an individual who sins by following בית דין's mistaken ruling does not bring his own קרבן. שמואל says this is only רבי יהודה's opinion. According to חכמים, that individual still brings his own קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion
An individual, one person
A ruling of the court
Liable (here, he must bring a קרבן)

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the sugya is built around finding the source for each side of this מחלוקת.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: "This" means the משנה's rule that someone who follows בית דין's ruling is exempt.

phrases.english: but the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: יָחִיד שֶׁעָשָׂה בְּהוֹרָאַת בֵּית דִּין – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: An individual who acted on the ruling of the court is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: who holds the משנה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's exemption follows רבי יהודה; חכמים hold the individual is חייב.

steps.title: The source for רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי יהודה's view comes from and answers with a ברייתא: the פסוק has three limiting words, and one teaches that someone who follows בית דין is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי יהודה's view? As a ברייתא teaches: 'If one soul shall sin unwittingly in performing it.' These are three limiting words: one who acts on his own is liable, but one who acts on the ruling of בית דין is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which teaching shows רבי יהודה's opinion. It answers by quoting a ברייתא that learns from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'one,' 'unwittingly,' and 'in performing' each limit who must bring a קרבן. One of these limits teaches that the individual brings a קרבן only when he acted on his own. If he acted because בית דין told him to, he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Limiting words that exclude cases
Unwittingly, by mistake
On his own, by himself
Exempt

phrases.english: What is Rabbi Yehuda's view?
As it is taught in a baraita:
"If one soul shall sin unwittingly in performing it"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:27

phrases.english: these are three limiting terms:
phrases.notes: The three words are "one," "unwittingly," and "in performing."

phrases.english: one who acts on his own is liable,
but one who acts on the ruling of the court is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the first side of שמואל's מחלוקת.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that one who follows בית דין is פטור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading three limiting words in ויקרא 4:27.

steps.title: The source for the Sages' view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא for חכמים: 'מעם הארץ' teaches that even a majority, or the whole people, who sin through בית דין's ruling still bring their own קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the view of the רבנן? As a ברייתא teaches: I might still say that a minority of the congregation who sinned is liable, since בית דין does not bring a bull because of them. But a majority who sinned should be exempt, since בית דין does bring a bull because of them. So the פסוק says 'from among the people of the land': even most of them, and even all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show where חכמים's view comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first suggests a split. A minority brings its own קרבנות, because בית דין's communal bull does not cover them, while a majority might be exempt, because בית דין brings a bull for them. The פסוק 'מעם הארץ' rejects this and says even a majority, or all of them, are liable. The next steps ask exactly what case this ברייתא means, and only then draw the proof for חכמים (step 27).

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis (same as חכמים)
I might still say (a possible line of thought that will be rejected)
A minority of the congregation
A majority of the congregation
The bull brought by בית דין for a communal mistake
From among the people of the land

phrases.english: What is the view of the Rabbis?
As it is taught in a baraita: I might still say:
a minority of the congregation that sinned is liable,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין בֵּית דִּין מְבִיאִין עַל יְדֵיהֶן פַּר.
phrases.english: since the court does not bring a bull on their account.
A majority of the congregation that sinned should be exempt,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי בֵּית דִּין מְבִיאִין עַל יְדֵיהֶם פַּר.
phrases.english: since the court does bring a bull on their account.
So the verse says: "From among the people of the land"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:27

phrases.english: even most of it, and even all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי רַבָּנַן? דְּתַנְיָא, עֲדַיִין אֲנִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the second side of the מחלוקת.
steps.raayaObject: חכמים's view that one who follows בית דין is חייב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'מעם הארץ' as including even the majority or the whole people.

steps.title: What case is the ברייתא talking about? Not a sin without a ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of sin the ברייתא means. It cannot be a plain mistake with no ruling, because then בית דין would have nothing to do with it and would bring no bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: In what case? If you say it is an unwitting act, with בית דין giving no ruling, what does בית דין have to do with it? If there was no ruling from בית דין, does בית דין bring a bull without a ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts testing the ברייתא by asking what case it describes. It knocks out the first option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said בית דין brings a bull for the majority. בית דין's bull is only brought when בית דין gave a mistaken ruling. So the ברייתא cannot be talking about people who simply made a mistake on their own.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case?
If you say
An unwitting act done without any ruling
What do they have to do with it?

phrases.english: In what case? If you say with an unwitting act
[the court without a ruling],
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording; they make clear that בית דין gave no ruling here.

phrases.english: what does the court have to do with it?
If it was not by the ruling of the court,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית דִּין מִי מַיְיתוּ שֶׁלֹּא בְּהוֹרָאָה?
phrases.english: does the court bring a bull without a ruling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts examining the חכמים ברייתא from step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that בית דין brings a bull for the majority.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no ruling was given, בית דין never brings a bull, so the ברייתא's reasoning makes no sense in that case.

steps.title: But a case with a ruling doesn't fit the verse either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the other option, a sin done through a ruling. But the פסוק 'מעם הארץ' is written about a plain unwitting act, not a ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is talking about a sin through a ruling. But the פסוק 'from among the people of the land' is written about an unwitting act!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second option and finds a problem with it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא means people who sinned because of a ruling, it should not use 'מעם הארץ' as its proof. That פסוק is about an individual's plain mistake, not about following בית דין. Both readings now seem to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather
But surely
It is written

phrases.english: Rather, with a ruling.
But when "from among the people of the land" is written,
it is written about an unwitting act!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּהוֹרָאָה. וְהָא כִּי כְּתִיב מֵעַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the 'no ruling' option, the גמרא challenges the 'ruling' option.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the ברייתא as talking about a sin through a ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The proof-פסוק 'מעם הארץ' is about a plain unwitting act, so it cannot teach about a ruling.

steps.title: Re-reading the ברייתא: a minority who followed a ruling is liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-reads the ברייתא: a minority who sinned by a plain mistake is חייב, and since בית דין brings no bull for a minority even when it ruled, a minority who followed a ruling is also חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't this what it means: a minority of the congregation who sinned by an unwitting act is liable. Since בית דין does not bring a bull on their account when there was a ruling, those people are also liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the problem by reading the ברייתא's words in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'minority' part of the ברייתא is now about two cases. A minority who made a plain mistake is חייב, which fits 'מעם הארץ.' A minority who sinned through a ruling is also חייב, because בית דין's bull does not cover them. This seems to show the view of חכמים, but רב פפא will challenge the proof in step 25, and steps 26-27 defend it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that
This is what it means
So, these (people)

steps.whatToRemember: According to חכמים, a person who sins by following בית דין's mistaken ruling still brings his own קרבן, at least when he is part of a minority that בית דין's bull does not cover. רבי יהודה, followed by the משנה, says he is פטור.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that this is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: מִיעוּט קָהָל שֶׁחָטְאוּ בְּשִׁגְגַת מַעֲשֶׂה חַיָּיבִין,
phrases.english: a minority of the congregation that sinned with an unwitting act is liable,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין בֵּית דִּין מְבִיאִין עַל יְדֵיהֶן פַּר בְּהוֹרָאָה.
phrases.english: since the court does not bring a bull on their account with a ruling.
So they are liable.
phrases.notes: "They" means a minority who sinned through בית דין's ruling: they too must bring their own קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two challenges of steps 21 and 22 by re-reading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to describe only one kind of sin, and neither kind fit both its reasoning and its proof-פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא covers a minority's plain mistake, which fits 'מעם הארץ,' and teaches that a minority who followed a ruling is also חייב.

steps.title: The ברייתא's second line: even a majority is liable
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: one might have thought a majority who sinned through a plain mistake is פטור, because בית דין brings a bull for a majority when there was a ruling. 'מעם הארץ' teaches that even a majority is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think that if most of the people sinned by a plain mistake, they would be exempt, since בית דין brings a bull for them when there was a ruling. So the פסוק says 'from the people of the land': even the majority must bring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא for חכמים. This line deals with a majority who sinned by a plain mistake, not through any ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא raises a possible reason to exempt a majority: a majority is the group that triggers בית דין's bull when there is a ruling. 'מעם הארץ' rejects that reason. The גמרא will now use the fact that the ברייתא only worried about the majority, and not the minority, as the basis of its proof.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might have thought.' It brings up a mistaken idea that the פסוק comes to reject
The majority of the community
An unwitting act, a plain mistake with no ruling from בית דין behind it
The bull בית דין brings when the community sins by following its ruling
'The פסוק teaches.' It introduces the words of a פסוק that settle the question

phrases.english: One might think that a majority of the community
who acted through an unwitting act
would be exempt,
since the court brings, on their account,
a bull [when there was a ruling]?
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording. The bull only comes when בית דין gave a ruling.

phrases.english: The verse states: "From the people of the land,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:27

phrases.english: even its majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל רוֹב צִבּוּר שֶׁעָשׂוּ בְּשִׁגְגַת מַעֲשֶׂה יְהוּ פְּטוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that step 23 re-read, adding its line about the majority.
steps.raayaObject: That חכמים hold a minority who followed a ruling is חייב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's line about a majority who sinned by a plain mistake, learned from 'מעם הארץ'

steps.title: רב פפא: maybe nobody brings a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks how we know the minority who followed a ruling is חייב. Maybe in that case neither the people nor בית דין bring anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: How do you know that? Maybe in that case neither they nor בית דין bring a קרבן!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on the proof the גמרא just built. He suggests a third option for a minority who followed a ruling: complete exemption for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we assumed someone has to bring a קרבן. רב פפא says the people might be פטור because they relied on בית דין. בית דין might also be פטור, because only a minority sinned. If that is possible, the ברייתא proves nothing about a minority with a ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where?' How do you know this?
'Perhaps.' It offers another possible way to understand the case

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: From where do you know this?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא לֹא הֵן וְלֹא בֵּית דִּין!
phrases.english: Perhaps neither they nor the court bring an offering!
phrases.notes: He is talking about a minority who followed a ruling: maybe nobody brings a קרבן at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא לֹא הֵן וְלֹא בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion drawn from the ברייתא in steps 23 and 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that a minority who followed a ruling is חייב according to חכמים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof ignores a third option, that both the people and בית דין are exempt

steps.title: Why did the ברייתא jump straight to the majority?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רב פפא: if the minority-with-a-ruling case were unclear, the ברייתא would first have proven that a minority is חייב for a plain mistake, and only then the majority. Jumping to the majority shows the minority case was already obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the ברייתא bother specifically to prove the majority is liable? Doesn't that show it was already clear that a minority who followed a ruling is liable? Otherwise, let it first prove that a minority is liable for a plain mistake, and only at the end prove the majority is liable for a plain mistake!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against רב פפא by looking at what the ברייתא chose to discuss and what it left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a minority who followed a ruling were exempt, as רב פפא suggests, we could also wonder whether a minority who made a plain mistake is exempt. Then the ברייתא would have to prove the minority case first. Since it skipped right to the majority, it must have taken for granted that a minority is חייב even with a ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so.' If your idea is right, then there is a problem
'Why specifically this?' Why did the text pick this case?
Goes searching, makes an effort to prove something
By implication, from what is understood
A minority of the community

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not proving this from a word in the פסוק. It is proving it from the ORDER of the ברייתא: what the ברייתא bothered to discuss and what it skipped.

phrases.english: If so, why specifically
does he go seeking a proof about the majority being liable?
phrases.notes: 'He' means the author of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Is it not by implication that, about a minority with a ruling,
it is settled for him that they are liable with a ruling?!
Otherwise, let him first seek a proof about a minority
that it is liable for an unwitting act,
and only at the end seek a proof about the majority
being liable for an unwitting act!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַאי אִירְיָא דְּקָמְהַדַּר עַל רוּבָּא לְחִיּוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפא's suggestion in step 25 by using the structure of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's suggestion that a minority who followed a ruling is completely exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were possible, the ברייתא should first have proven that a minority is liable for a plain mistake. Its skipping straight to the majority shows the minority case was obvious.

steps.title: Conclusion: a minority is liable with or without a ruling
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא did not prove the minority case first and went straight to the majority, we learn that a minority who followed a ruling is חייב and brings a female lamb or goat. A minority who sinned without a ruling, through a plain mistake, is also חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since the ברייתא did not seek a proof that a minority is liable for a plain mistake, and only sought a proof that the majority is liable for a plain mistake, learn from this: a minority who followed a ruling is liable, and each brings a female lamb or goat. Without a ruling, through a plain mistake, they are also liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the argument against רב פפא and states the result for חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The silence of the ברייתא about the minority case is the proof. For a minority, a ruling changes nothing: each person brings his own קרבן whether or not בית דין ruled. This is the opposite of רבי יהודה, who holds that someone who follows בית דין is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, is it not so that...' It leads into the conclusion
'Learn from it.' This is the conclusion
A female lamb or female goat, the individual's חטאת
Without a ruling from בית דין

steps.whatToRemember: According to חכמים, a minority who sinned by following בית דין's ruling is חייב, just like a minority who made a plain mistake. Each one brings his own female lamb or goat.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out the view of חכמים against רבי יהודה (step 19). Relying on בית דין does not exempt an individual when only a minority sinned.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not so: since he did not seek a proof
about a minority being liable for an unwitting act,
and in the end he did seek a proof about the majority
being liable for an unwitting act.
Learn from this: a minority with a ruling is liable;
they bring a female lamb or a female goat,
and without a ruling,
for an unwitting act, they are liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו מִדְּלָא מְהַדַּר עַל מִיעוּט דְּמִיחַיְּיבִין בְּשִׁגְגַת מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from the question in step 26, rejecting רב פפא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to חכמים, a minority is חייב a female lamb or goat whether it sinned by following a ruling or by a plain mistake.

steps.title: Both teachings are unnamed, so maybe the authors are reversed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that the first ברייתא is רבי יהודה and the second is the רבנן. Both were taught without names, so why not say the opposite?
steps.simpleTranslation: Look, both ברייתות were taught anonymously. How do we know the first one is רבי יהודה and the second one is the רבנן? Say it the other way around!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how we decided which ברייתא belongs to רבי יהודה and which to the רבנן, since neither one names its author.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא settled the clash between the two ברייתות by giving each one a different author. Now it attacks that move: nothing in the text tells us who said which. If we swap them, the first ברייתא, which exempts a person who followed a ruling, would be the רבנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Look now / since it is so: opens a point based on known facts
Unattributed: taught without naming who said it
The first one (here, the first ברייתא)
The latter one (the second ברייתא)
Say the opposite: maybe it is reversed

phrases.english: Now, we learned both of them unattributed;
phrases.notes: 'Both of them' means the two ברייתות the גמרא has been comparing.

phrases.english: from where do we know that the first is רבי יהודה
and the latter is the Rabbis?
Say the opposite!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that the second ברייתא makes a minority who followed a ruling חייב, the גמרא questions the author assignments that let the two ברייתות not contradict each other.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assignment of the first ברייתא to רבי יהודה and the second to the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both ברייתות are anonymous, so there is no clear basis for this assignment. The reverse is just as possible.

steps.title: Reading exclusion words this way is רבי יהודה's style
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the first ברייתא learns rules from exclusion words, and that style of reading belongs to רבי יהודה. It begins quoting a ברייתא to prove it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who have you heard reads exclusion words like this? It is רבי יהודה, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we can tell who wrote the first ברייתא from how it reads the פסוק. It is setting up a quote from a ברייתא where רבי יהודה reads that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא learns its rule from small 'limiting' words in the פסוק (מיעוטים). The גמרא says this way of reading is known to be רבי יהודה's. That is why the first ברייתא is his and not the רבנן's, and the proof comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Have you heard him: do we know someone who holds this?
Interprets / expounds a פסוק
Exclusions: words in a פסוק that limit or leave out a case
In this way / like this

phrases.notes: 'In this way' points back to how the first ברייתא learned its rule from limiting words in the פסוק.

phrases.english: It is רבי יהודה,
as it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says:

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּדָרֵישׁ מִיעוּטֵי כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28 by identifying the author from his known way of reading פסוקים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the author by his known method of reading פסוקים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since both ברייתות are anonymous, either one could belong to רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first ברייתא reads exclusion words, which is רבי יהודה's known method, so it is his. The second belongs to the רבנן.
